english.title: Transport for sale dead non-Schedule 1 wild bird
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person who was not registered for the purpose, transported for the purpose of sale

(A)_[a dead wild bird,]_
(B)_[dead wild birds,]_
(C)_[part or parts of or anything derived from a dead wild bird,]_
(D)_[parts of or anything derived from dead wild birds,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY SPECIES..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(2)(a) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

sale
non-schedule 1 dead wild bird(s) or

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Does not apply to birds listed in Part II or III of Schedule 3 to the Act.
(ii) See Section 27 for meaning of "sale" and "wild bird".
(iii) See Section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
(iv) See Section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(v) As amended by paragraph 10 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.
(vi) See offence wordings H4602, H4603 and H4604.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one bird is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each bird (Section 21(5)).

Complex - see legislation
